content: 1. The relationship between self-rated functional ability and self-rated health was examined in relation to concurrent functional capacity, functional decline, and mortality. These findings were derived from the Nun Study and published in The Journals of Gerontology Series B: Psychological Sciences and Social Sciences in 1996 (Volume 51, Issue 5, Pages S234–S241). 2. Heywood F. explored the cost-effectiveness and value of housing adaptations in his book Money Well Spent: The Effectiveness and Value of Housing Adaptations, published by Policy Press, Bristol, in 2001. Additionally, Heywood F. investigated the health outcomes associated with housing adaptations in the article published in Disability & Society in 2004 (Volume 19, Issue 2, Pages 129–143). 3. Humpel N., Owen N., and Leslie E. conducted a review of environmental factors influencing adults' participation in physical activity. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2002 (Volume 22, Issue 3, Pages 188–199). 4. Joshu C., Boehmer T., Brownson R., and Ewing R. analyzed personal, neighborhood, and urban factors associated with obesity in the United States. Their study was published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health in 2008 (Volume 62, Issue 3, Pages 202–208). 5. Katz S., Amasa B. Ford, Roland W. Moskowitz, Beverly A. Jackson, and Marjorie W. conducted seminal studies on illness in the aged, published in the Journal of the American Medical Association in 1963 (Volume 185, Pages 94–99). Katz S. also developed methods for assessing self-maintenance activities, including activities of daily living, mobility, and instrumental activities of daily living, as published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Association in 1983 (Volume 31, Pages 721–727). 6. Lakdawalla D., Goldman D.P., Bhattacharya J., Hurd M.D., Joyce G.F., and Panis C.W. forecasted the nursing home population in their study published in Medical Care in 2003 (Volume 41, Issue 1, Pages 8–20). 7. Law M., Baptiste S., McColl M., Opzoomer A., Polatajko H., and Pollock N. introduced the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure as an outcome measure for occupational therapy. This was published in the Canadian Journal of Occupational Therapy in 1990 (Volume 57, Issue 2, Pages 82–87). 8. Lawton M.P. and Brody E. developed an assessment framework for older adults focusing on self-maintenance and instrumental activities of daily living. This was published in The Gerontologist in 1969 (Volume 9, Pages 179–186). Lawton M.P. also explored the social ecology and health of older adults in the American Journal of Public Health in 1974 (Volume 64, Issue 3, Pages 257–260). 9. Maggi P., de Almeida Mello J., Delye S., et al. examined fall determinants and home modifications implemented by occupational therapists to prevent falls. Their findings were published in the Canadian Journal of Occupational Therapy in 2018 (Volume 85, Issue 1, Pages 79–87). 10. Meader N., King K., Llewellyn A., et al. developed a checklist to ensure consistency and reproducibility in GRADE assessments. This was published in Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Volume 3, Article 1). 11. Norin L., Slaug B., Haak M., et al. investigated housing accessibility and its association with participation among older adults with long-standing spinal cord injuries. Their study was published in The Journal of Spinal Cord Medicine in 2017 (Volume 40, Issue 2, Pages 230–240). 12. Petersson I., Kottorp A., Bergstrom J., and Lilja M. studied longitudinal changes in daily life following home modifications for aging individuals with disabilities. This was published in the Scandinavian Journal of Occupational Therapy in 2009 (Volume 16, Issue 2, Pages 78–87). 13. Petersson I., Lilja M., Hammel J., and Kottorp A. evaluated the impact of home modification services on daily life abilities for aging individuals with disabilities. Their findings were published in the Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine in 2008 (Volume 40, Issue 4, Pages 253–260). 14. Pluye P., Gagnon M.-P., Griffiths F., and Johnson-Lafleur J. proposed a scoring system for appraising mixed-methods research in systematic reviews. This was published in the International Journal of Nursing Studies in 2009 (Volume 46, Issue 4, Pages 529–546). 15. Saville-Smith K. and Fraser R. addressed housing and disability, emphasizing the need to future-proof New Zealand's housing stock for inclusivity. This was published by the Centre for Housing Research, Aotearoa New Zealand, in 2007. 16. Schünemann H.J., Oxman A.D., Vist G.E., et al. provided guidance on interpreting results and drawing conclusions in systematic reviews, as outlined in Chapter 12 of the Cochrane Handbook (updated March 2011). 17. Slaug B., Chiatti C., Oswald F., et al. analyzed the short-term costs and long-term benefits of improved housing accessibility for older adults in Sweden and Germany. Their study was published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in 2017 (Volume 14, Article 964). 18. Smith S.K., Rayer S., and Smith E.A. explored the implications of aging and disability for the housing industry and policy in the United States. This was published in the Journal of the American Planning Association in 2008 (Volume 74, Issue 3, Pages 289–306). 19. Stark S. demonstrated that removing environmental barriers in the homes of older adults with disabilities improves occupational performance. This was published in OTJR: Occupation, Participation, and Health in 2004 (Volume 24, Issue 1, Pages 32–39). 20. Stineman M.G., Ross R.N., Maislin G., and Gray D. conducted a population-based study on home accessibility features and their impact on activities of daily living. Their findings were published in Disability & Rehabilitation in 2007 (Volume 29, Issue 15, Pages 1165–1175). 21. Tchalla A.E., Lachal F., Cardinaud N., et al. evaluated the efficacy of simple home-based technologies combined with monitoring centers in reducing falls among frail elderly populations. This was part of the ESOPPE study, published in Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics in 2012 (Volume 55, Issue 3, Pages 683–689). 22. Thomas H., Weaver N., Patterson J., et al. examined the relationship between mental health and the quality of residential environments. Their study was published in The British Journal of Psychiatry in 2007 (Volume 191, Issue 6, Pages 500–505). 23. Tongsiri S., Ploylearmsang C., Hawsutisima K., et al. discussed home modifications for individuals with physical disabilities in Thailand. This was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2017 (Volume 95, Pages 140–145). 24. The United Nations published a report on global population aging from 1950 to 2050, emphasizing demographic trends and their implications. This was released in 2002. 25. The United Nations adopted the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and Optional Protocol in 2006, establishing a framework for the rights of individuals with disabilities. 26. Van Hoof J., Kort H., Van Waarde H., and Blom M. reviewed environmental interventions and home designs for older adults with dementia. This was published in the American Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease and Other Dementias in 2010 (Volume 25, Issue 3, Pages 202–232). 27. Whiteford G. highlighted occupational deprivation as a global challenge in the new millennium. This was published in The British Journal of Occupational Therapy in 2000 (Volume 63, Issue 5, Pages 200–204). 28. The World Health Organization released a fact sheet on disability and health in December 2014, providing key statistics and insights into global disability trends. 29. The World Health Organization also published the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) in 2002, aiming to establish a common language for understanding disability and health.
